edges.description: Disturbed keratinocyte architecture and melanosome handling from KRT5 haploinsufficiency manifest as reticulate flexural hyperpigmentation.
Impaired O-fucosylation and O-glucosylation of Notch receptors by POFUT1 and POGLUT1 reduces canonical Notch signaling in epidermal keratinocytes and melanocytes.

edges.description: Impaired gamma-secretase-mediated intracellular cleavage of Notch receptors in PSENEN mutation carriers reduces Notch signaling in keratinocytes and melanocytes.

edges.description: Impaired gamma-secretase Notch cleavage in PSENEN mutation carriers produces follicular hyperkeratosis in hair follicles.
PSENEN loss-of-function variants confer susceptibility to comorbid acne inversa via follicular hyperkeratosis in the presence of predisposing trigger factors such as nicotine use or obesity.
Reduced epidermal and melanocytic Notch signaling disturbs melanin synthesis and distribution, producing reticulate flexural hyperpigmentation.

edges.description: Disrupted Notch-dependent melanin synthesis and distribution leads to hypopigmented macules alongside reticulate hyperpigmentation.

nodes.description: Acne inversa (hidradenitis suppurativa), an inflammatory hair-follicle disorder, can co-occur in a genotype-dependent subset, notably PSENEN mutation carriers.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in gamma-secretase subunit-encoding PSENEN underlie Dowling-Degos disease associated with acne inversa.
evidence.snippet: Six of the PSENEN mutation carriers presented with comorbid acne inversa (AI), an inflammatory hair follicle disorder, and had a history of nicotine abuse and/or obesity, which are known trigger factors for AI.

nodes.description: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in KRT5 reduce keratin 5 available for the basal keratinocyte intermediate-filament cytoskeleton. Functional studies implicate keratins in cell adhesion, melanosome uptake, organelle transport, and nuclear anchorage, so KRT5 haploinsufficiency is thought to disturb epidermal architecture and melanosome handling, producing the characteristic reticulate hyperpigmentation.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in the keratin 5 gene lead to Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: These represent the first identified mutations that lead to haploinsufficiency in a keratin gene.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in the keratin 5 gene lead to Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: The identification of loss-of-function mutations, along with the results from additional functional studies, suggest a crucial role for keratins in the organization of cell adhesion, melanosome uptake, organelle transport, and nuclear anchorage.

nodes.description: Follicular hyperkeratosis, a histopathologic feature that in PSENEN-associated disease distinguished carriers from other DDD patients.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in gamma-secretase subunit-encoding PSENEN underlie Dowling-Degos disease associated with acne inversa.
evidence.snippet: Further examination revealed that the histopathologic feature of follicular hyperkeratosis distinguished these 6 patients from previously studied individuals with DDD.

nodes.description: Heterozygous truncating variants in PSENEN impair presenilin enhancer protein 2 (PEN-2), a subunit of the gamma-secretase complex required for intramembrane cleavage of Notch receptors and activation of intracellular Notch signaling in the epidermis and hair follicle.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in gamma-secretase subunit-encoding PSENEN underlie Dowling-Degos disease associated with acne inversa.
evidence.snippet: PSENEN encodes presenilin enhancer protein 2 (PEN-2), a member of the γ -secretase enzyme complex, which is responsible for the intracellular cleavage of Notch receptors that is necessary for the activation of Notch signaling

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in gamma-secretase subunit-encoding PSENEN underlie Dowling-Degos disease associated with acne inversa.
evidence.snippet: Here, we have identified 6 heterozygous truncating mutations in PSENEN, encoding presenilin enhancer protein 2, in 6 unrelated patients and families with DDD in whom mutations in KRT5, POFUT1, and POGLUT1 have been excluded.

nodes.description: Hypopigmented macules interspersed with the reticulate hyperpigmentation of the flexures.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in POFUT1, encoding protein O-fucosyltransferase 1, cause generalized Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: characterized by reticular hyperpigmentation and hypopigmentation of the flexures

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in the keratin 5 gene lead to Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: We identified loss-of-function mutations in the keratin 5 gene (KRT5) in all affected family members and in six unrelated patients with DDD.

nodes.description: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in POFUT1 and POGLUT1 impair addition of O-linked fucose and O-linked glucose to epidermal growth factor-like repeats of Notch receptors, reducing Notch receptor activation in keratinocytes and melanocytes.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in POGLUT1, encoding protein O-glucosyltransferase 1, cause autosomal-dominant Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: Interestingly, both POGLUT1 and POFUT1 are essential regulators of Notch activity.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in POFUT1, encoding protein O-fucosyltransferase 1, cause generalized Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: Knockdown of POFUT1 reduces the expression of NOTCH1, NOTCH2, HES1, and KRT5 in HaCaT cells.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in POFUT1, encoding protein O-fucosyltransferase 1, cause generalized Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: Our findings demonstrate that POFUT1 mutations cause generalized DDD.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in POFUT1, encoding protein O-fucosyltransferase 1, cause generalized Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: Morpholino knockdown of pofut1 in zebrafish produced a phenotype characteristic of hypopigmentation at 48 hr postfertilization (hpf) and abnormal melanin distribution at 72 hpf, replicating the clinical phenotype observed in our DDD individuals.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in POGLUT1, encoding protein O-glucosyltransferase 1, cause autosomal-dominant Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: These mutations, namely c.11G>A (p.Trp4*), c.652C>T (p.Arg218*), and c.798-2A>C, are within POGLUT1, which encodes protein O-glucosyltransferase 1.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in gamma-secretase subunit-encoding PSENEN underlie Dowling-Degos disease associated with acne inversa.
evidence.snippet: Here, we have identified 6 heterozygous truncating mutations in PSENEN, encoding presenilin enhancer protein 2, in 6 unrelated patients and families with DDD in whom mutations in KRT5, POFUT1, and POGLUT1 have been excluded.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in gamma-secretase subunit-encoding PSENEN underlie Dowling-Degos disease associated with acne inversa.
evidence.snippet: Knockdown of psenen in zebrafish larvae resulted in a phenotype with scattered pigmentation that mimicked human DDD.

nodes.description: Attenuated Notch signaling in epidermal keratinocytes and melanocytes disrupts melanin synthesis, melanosome transfer, and keratinocyte differentiation, producing reticulate hyperpigmentation and hypopigmented macules.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in POGLUT1, encoding protein O-glucosyltransferase 1, cause autosomal-dominant Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: Our results furthermore emphasize the important role of the Notch pathway in pigmentation and keratinocyte morphology.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in POFUT1, encoding protein O-fucosyltransferase 1, cause generalized Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: These results strongly suggest that the protein product of POFUT1 plays a significant and conserved role in melanin synthesis and transport.

nodes.description: Progressive, disfiguring net-like (reticulate) hyperpigmentation involving the flexural sites (axillae, groin, neck, inframammary regions).

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in the keratin 5 gene lead to Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: Dowling-Degos disease (DDD) is an autosomal dominant genodermatosis characterized by progressive and disfiguring reticulate hyperpigmentation of the flexures.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in POFUT1, encoding protein O-fucosyltransferase 1, cause generalized Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: characterized by reticular hyperpigmentation and hypopigmentation of the flexures, such as the neck, axilla, and areas below the breasts and groin
